Show images, video and audio

Display an image, play a video, or add audio to your window. Packaged Minecraft images can be drawn directly. For a file or stream, open a MediaPlayer, update it from client callbacks, and close it when its screen finishes.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or settingArgumentsWhat it does
MediaPlayer.open(source, kind, options, decoder)Media source; media kind; playback options; decoderUse the built-in decoder for supported images/audio, or an explicitly installed FFmpeg executable for video and animated images.
volume(value)Playback volumeThe example uses 0.25 for quieter audio.
play() / pause() / seek(seconds)Playback action; seek position in secondsStart or resume the clock, pause it, or move to another point.
draw(x, y, width, height, opacity)Destination rectangle and opacityDraw from the client render callback. A false result lets your screen show loading or failure feedback.

When you finish: Call update from client tick/render callbacks, including for audio-only playback. Close the player in screen disposal, or attach it to its window with ownVisual. Packaged Minecraft textures belong to the texture manager and must not be deleted by the screen.

Image from your addon · Still image · Animated GIF · Video · Custom audio player

Display an image

Put a 256 × 256 PNG at src/main/resources/assets/example/textures/gui/logo.png. The example reads the full 256 × 256 source image and draws it in a 64 × 64 rectangle in Minecraft GUI units. To display it in Java, Kotlin, Scala or GroovyScript, call the drawing method from your screen’s render callback on the client thread. In CraftTweaker, add the image to the screen declaration. Minecraft’s texture manager owns this cached texture, so do not delete it when the window closes. For a file chosen at runtime, use the still-image player below. Animated GIFs need the separate playback recipe.

import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui;
import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation;

final class PackagedImage {
    private static final ResourceLocation LOGO =
            new ResourceLocation("example", "textures/gui/logo.png");

    // Called from your screen's render callback. The source image is 256 x 256.
    static void draw(int x, int y) {
        Minecraft.getMinecraft().getTextureManager().bindTexture(LOGO);
        Gui.drawScaledCustomSizeModalRect(x, y, 0, 0, 256, 256, 64, 64, 256, 256);
    }
}

import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;

function openImageWindow() as Window {

Choose a decoder

MediaDecoders.builtin() uses installed ImageIO readers for still images and Java Sound providers for audio. Video and animated images need a video decoder. MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(path) uses an explicitly configured FFmpeg executable for images, animated images, video and audio. Offscreen does not bundle or download that executable. Its supported formats depend on the codecs enabled in that build; see FFmpeg's format reference. Other decoders can implement MediaDecoder without changing the player API.

A filename extension is not a guarantee of a codec. Unsupported, corrupt or missing media produces FAILED with a retained cause. The player never silently claims that an unknown format was decoded. DRM-protected media and interactive formats such as HTML are not generic video streams.

Play a video

Client setup: retain a player for this screen instance. The decoding worker prepares it; play() starts the playback clock. Drawing returns false while loading or after failure, so your screen can show useful feedback. Call update() in a client tick/render callback even for audio-only players so end/loop handling runs. Window readiness and media readiness are separate.

import java.nio.file.Path;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.media.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

final class MediaRecipe {
    private final MediaPlayer video;
    // Client setup: ffmpeg and clip are paths chosen by your addon/user.
    MediaRecipe(Window window, Path ffmpeg, Path clip) {
        video = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
                MediaSource.Kind.VIDEO, MediaOptions.defaults(), MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(ffmpeg)));
        video.volume(.25);
        video.play();
    }
    // Render callback: false means no frame is available; draw your loading/error label then.
    boolean draw(int width, int height) { return video.draw(0, 0, width, height, 1); }
    void pause() { video.pause(); }
    void resume() { video.play(); }
    void jumpTo(double seconds) { video.seek(seconds); }
    MediaPlayer.Status status() { return video.status(); }
    // Client teardown: the window also closes this exact player if you leave it installed.
    void dispose() { video.close(); }
}

import java.nio.file.Path

class MediaKotlin(window: Window, ffmpeg: Path, clip: Path) {
    private val video = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
        MediaSource.Kind.VIDEO, MediaOptions.defaults(), MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(ffmpeg)))
    init { video.volume(.25); video.play() }
    // Client render callback: show your loading/error label when this returns false.
    fun draw(width: Int, height: Int) = video.draw(0.0, 0.0, width.toDouble(), height.toDouble(), 1f)
    fun pause() { video.pause() }
    fun resume() { video.play() }
    fun jumpTo(seconds: Double) { video.seek(seconds) }
    fun status(): MediaPlayer.Status = video.status()
    fun dispose() { video.close() }
}

#side client
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Media;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.MediaPlayer;

// Call from a client action after you have a window and configured file/executable paths.
function openVideo(window as Window, ffmpeg as string, clip as string) as MediaPlayer {
    val video = Media.open(window, Media.file(clip), "video", ffmpeg,
        Media.options(640, 360, 30, true, false));
    video.volume(0.25);
    video.play();
    return video;
}
// Render callback: display your loading/error label when this returns false.
function drawVideo(video as MediaPlayer, width as int, height as int) as bool {
    return video.draw(0, 0, width, height, 1);
}
function pauseVideo(video as MediaPlayer) { video.pause(); }
function resumeVideo(video as MediaPlayer) { video.play(); }
function jumpTo(video as MediaPlayer, seconds as double) { video.seek(seconds); }
function inspectVideo(video as MediaPlayer) {
    if (video.error != "") print(video.error);
    if (video.audioError != "") print(video.audioError);
}
function disposeVideo(video as MediaPlayer) { video.close(); }

Display an image from a file

Keep one player per screen. ImageIO decodes the image in the background; draw it in your screen’s render callback. A false draw result means the texture is not available yet: show a loading label, or the retained error if loading failed. Close it from screen teardown. This recipe uses the built-in decoder and needs no FFmpeg executable.

import java.nio.file.Path;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.media.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

final class StillImage {
    private final MediaPlayer image;
    // The source path belongs to this screen instance.
    StillImage(Window window, Path clip) {
        image = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
                MediaSource.Kind.IMAGE, MediaOptions.defaults(), MediaDecoders.builtin()));
        image.play();
    }
    // Render callback: false means no frame is available; draw your loading/error label then.
    boolean draw(int width, int height) { return image.draw(0, 0, width, height, 1); }
    MediaPlayer.Status status() { return image.status(); }
    // Client teardown: the window also closes this exact player if you leave it installed.
    void dispose() { image.close(); }
}

Play an animated GIF

Treat the GIF as VIDEO so its frame timestamps are played, rather than reading only its first still frame. This uses an existing FFmpeg executable, disables audio and loops. Draw from the client render callback; close the player when the screen is disposed. Pause and seek apply to this player independently of other windows.

import java.nio.file.Path;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.media.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;

final class AnimatedGif {
    private final MediaPlayer animation;
    // The source path belongs to this screen instance.
    AnimatedGif(Window window, Path ffmpeg, Path clip) {
        animation = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
                MediaSource.Kind.VIDEO, new MediaOptions(640, 360, 24, false, true, 256 * 1024 * 1024), MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(ffmpeg)));
        animation.play();
    }
    // Render callback: false means no frame is available; draw your loading/error label then.
    boolean draw(int width, int height) { return animation.draw(0, 0, width, height, 1); }
    void pause() { animation.pause(); }
    void resume() { animation.play(); }
    void jumpTo(double seconds) { animation.seek(seconds); }
    MediaPlayer.Status status() { return animation.status(); }
    // Client teardown: the window also closes this exact player if you leave it installed.
    void dispose() { animation.close(); }
}

Create a custom audio player

Build a compact audio interface with play/pause, ten-second seeking, mute and a volume bar. The bar controls volume, not playback progress; the decoder does not provide a reliable duration for every source. This layout needs at least 300 × 100 logical pixels. Java, Kotlin, Scala and Groovy install a GuiScreen in the window you pass to the constructor; VanillaUI connects its drawing and mouse input to that window. CraftTweaker declares the same drawing and input callbacks on its screen. Keep the returned window and close it during teardown. The player is closed both by screen disposal and its owning window, safely. Check the retained error when “Audio unavailable” is shown. The screen runs on the client thread; audio decoding and output run in the background.

import java.nio.file.Path;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.media.*;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI;
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window;
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen;

final class MinimalAudio extends GuiScreen {
    private final MediaPlayer audio;
    private double volume = 0.5;
    private boolean muted;

    MinimalAudio(Window window, Path ffmpeg, Path clip) {
        audio = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
                MediaSource.Kind.AUDIO, MediaOptions.defaults(), MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(ffmpeg)));
        audio.volume(volume);
        audio.play();
        window.setUI(new VanillaUI(this));
    }

    @Override public void drawScreen(int x, int y, float partial) {
        audio.update();
        var status = audio.status();
        drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF10141C);
        drawString(fontRenderer, status.failure() == null
                ? status.state() + " / " + (int) status.seconds() + " s" : "Audio unavailable", 12, 12, 0xFFE5EDF7);
        String[] labels = {status.state() == MediaPlayer.State.PLAYING ? "Pause" : "Play", "-10 s", "+10 s", muted ? "Unmute" : "Mute"};
        for (int i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
            int left = 12 + i * 70;
            drawRect(left, 34, left + 62, 58, 0xFF263346);
            drawString(fontRenderer, labels[i], left + 6, 42, 0xFFE5EDF7);
        }
        drawRect(12, 76, 284, 80, 0xFF263346);
        drawRect(12, 76, 12 + (int) (272 * volume), 80, 0xFF77C8E8);
    }

    @Override protected void mouseClicked(int x, int y, int button) {
        if (button != 0) return;
        if (y >= 70 && y < 88 && x >= 12 && x < 284) {
            volume = (x - 12) / 272.0;
            audio.volume(volume);
        } else if (y >= 34 && y < 58 && x >= 12 && x < 284) {
            int action = (x - 12) / 70;
            if ((x - 12) % 70 >= 62) return;
            if (action == 0) { if (audio.status().state() == MediaPlayer.State.PLAYING) audio.pause(); else audio.play(); }
            if (action == 1) audio.seek(Math.max(0, audio.status().seconds() - 10));
            if (action == 2) audio.seek(audio.status().seconds() + 10);
            if (action == 3) { muted = !muted; audio.muted(muted); }
        }
    }

    @Override public void onGuiClosed() { audio.close(); }
    @Override public boolean doesGuiPauseGame() { return false; }
}

import java.nio.file.Path
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.media.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen

class MinimalAudioKotlin(window: Window, ffmpeg: Path, clip: Path) : GuiScreen() {
    private val audio = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
        MediaSource.Kind.AUDIO, MediaOptions.defaults(), MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(ffmpeg)))
    private var volume = 0.5
    private var muted = false

    init {
        audio.volume(volume)
        audio.play()
        window.setUI(VanillaUI(this))
    }

    override fun drawScreen(x: Int, y: Int, partial: Float) {
        audio.update()
        val status = audio.status()
        drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF10141C.toInt())
        drawString(fontRenderer, if (status.failure() == null)
            "${status.state()} / ${status.seconds().toInt()} s" else "Audio unavailable", 12, 12, 0xFFE5EDF7.toInt())
        val labels = arrayOf(if (status.state() == MediaPlayer.State.PLAYING) "Pause" else "Play",
            "-10 s", "+10 s", if (muted) "Unmute" else "Mute")
        labels.forEachIndexed { i, label ->
            val left = 12 + i * 70
            drawRect(left, 34, left + 62, 58, 0xFF263346.toInt())
            drawString(fontRenderer, label, left + 6, 42, 0xFFE5EDF7.toInt())
        }
        drawRect(12, 76, 284, 80, 0xFF263346.toInt())
        drawRect(12, 76, 12 + (272 * volume).toInt(), 80, 0xFF77C8E8.toInt())
    }

    override fun mouseClicked(x: Int, y: Int, button: Int) {
        if (button != 0) return
        if (y in 70 until 88 && x in 12 until 284) {
            volume = (x - 12) / 272.0
            audio.volume(volume)
        } else if (y in 34 until 58 && x in 12 until 284) {
            if ((x - 12) % 70 >= 62) return
            when ((x - 12) / 70) {
                0 -> if (audio.status().state() == MediaPlayer.State.PLAYING) audio.pause() else audio.play()
                1 -> audio.seek(maxOf(0.0, audio.status().seconds() - 10))
                2 -> audio.seek(audio.status().seconds() + 10)
                3 -> { muted = !muted; audio.muted(muted) }
            }
        }
    }

    override fun onGuiClosed() { audio.close() }
    override fun doesGuiPauseGame() = false
}

        }
    }

    @Override public void onGuiClosed() { audio.close(); }
    @Override public boolean doesGuiPauseGame() { return false; }
}

import java.nio.file.Path
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.client.media.*
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.vanilla.VanillaUI
import com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Window
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen

final class MinimalAudioScala(window: Window, ffmpeg: Path, clip: Path) extends GuiScreen:
  private val audio = window.ownVisual(MediaPlayer.open(MediaSource.file(clip),
    MediaSource.Kind.AUDIO, MediaOptions.defaults(), MediaDecoders.ffmpeg(ffmpeg)))
  private var volume = 0.5
  private var muted = false
  audio.volume(volume)
  audio.play()
  window.setUI(new VanillaUI(this))

  override def drawScreen(x: Int, y: Int, partial: Float): Unit =
    audio.update()
    val status = audio.status()
    net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui.drawRect(0, 0, width, height, 0xFF10141C)
    val message = if status.failure() == null then s"${status.state()} / ${status.seconds().toInt} s" else "Audio unavailable"
    drawString(fontRenderer, message, 12, 12, 0xFFE5EDF7)
    val labels = Array(if status.state() == MediaPlayer.State.PLAYING then "Pause" else "Play",
      "-10 s", "+10 s", if muted then "Unmute" else "Mute")
    labels.zipWithIndex.foreach { (label, i) =>
      val left = 12 + i * 70
      net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui.drawRect(left, 34, left + 62, 58, 0xFF263346)
      drawString(fontRenderer, label, left + 6, 42, 0xFFE5EDF7)
    }
    net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui.drawRect(12, 76, 284, 80, 0xFF263346)
    net.minecraft.client.gui.Gui.drawRect(12, 76, 12 + (272 * volume).toInt, 80, 0xFF77C8E8)

  override protected def mouseClicked(x: Int, y: Int, button: Int): Unit =
    if button == 0 then
      if y >= 70 && y < 88 && x >= 12 && x < 284 then
        volume = (x - 12) / 272.0
        audio.volume(volume)
      else if y >= 34 && y < 58 && x >= 12 && x < 284 && (x - 12) % 70 < 62 then
        (x - 12) / 70 match
          case 0 => if audio.status().state() == MediaPlayer.State.PLAYING then audio.pause() else audio.play()
          case 1 => audio.seek(math.max(0, audio.status().seconds() - 10))
          case 2 => audio.seek(audio.status().seconds() + 10)
          case 3 => muted = !muted; audio.muted(muted)
          case _ => ()

  override def onGuiClosed(): Unit = audio.close()
  override def doesGuiPauseGame(): Boolean = false

#side client
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Windows;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Window;
import mods.offscreencleanroom.Media;

function openAudio(ffmpeg as string, clip as string) as Window {
    val screen = Windows.screen("Audio", 300, 100);
    val window = Windows.open(screen);
    val audio = Media.open(window, Media.file(clip), "audio", ffmpeg,
        Media.options(1, 1, 1, true, false));
    audio.volume(0.5);
    audio.play();
    screen.on("draw", function(e) {
        audio.update();
        if (!e.state.flag("initialized")) {
            e.state.integer("volume", 136);
            e.state.flag("initialized", true);
        }
        e.rect(0, 0, e.width, e.height, 0xFF10141C);
        e.text(audio.error == "" ? audio.state + " / " + audio.position as int + " s" : "Audio unavailable",
            12, 12, 0xFFE5EDF7, false);
        val labels = [audio.state == "PLAYING" ? "Pause" : "Play", "-10 s", "+10 s",
            e.state.flag("muted") ? "Unmute" : "Mute"] as string[];
        for i in 0 .. 4 {
            val left = 12 + i * 70;
            e.rect(left, 34, 62, 24, 0xFF263346);
            e.text(labels[i], left + 6, 42, 0xFFE5EDF7, false);
        }
        e.rect(12, 76, 272, 4, 0xFF263346);
        e.rect(12, 76, e.state.integer("volume"), 4, 0xFF77C8E8);
    });
    screen.on("click", function(e) {
        if (e.code != 0) return;
        if (e.y >= 70 && e.y < 88 && e.x >= 12 && e.x < 284) {
            val level = e.x - 12;
            e.state.integer("volume", level);
            audio.volume(level / 272.0);
        } else if (e.y >= 34 && e.y < 58 && e.x >= 12 && e.x < 284) {
            if ((e.x - 12) % 70 >= 62) return;
            val action = (e.x - 12) / 70;
            if (action == 0) { if (audio.state == "PLAYING") audio.pause(); else audio.play(); }
            if (action == 1) audio.seek(audio.position < 10 ? 0 : audio.position - 10);
            if (action == 2) audio.seek(audio.position + 10);
            if (action == 3) {
                val muted = !e.state.flag("muted");
                e.state.flag("muted", muted);
                audio.muted(muted);
            }
        }
    });
    screen.on("close", function(e) { audio.close(); });
    return window;
}

Choose a media source

Replace MediaSource.file(path) with resource(new ResourceLocation("example", "media/intro.mp4")) or url(URI.create(...)). ZenScript uses Media.file, Media.resource("example:media/intro.mp4") or Media.url. URL/resource inputs spool to a generation-owned temporary file for seeking, with a default 256 MiB encoded-size limit. Local files stream directly.

Use kind IMAGE for a still frame, AUDIO for sound only, and VIDEO for video or an animated GIF/WebP supported by the decoder. ZenScript accepts "image", "audio" and "video". Set audio false for silent playback; an audio-only player requires audio true. In ZenScript an empty executable path selects the built-in decoder. When using Java Sound, supported audio conversion depends on the installed providers.

Decoded images are fitted within the configured canvas with transparent letterboxing. Each player has independent pause, seek, mute and software volume. Java Sound output is separate from Minecraft's positional sound engine and its volume settings. A video can continue when an optional audio output device fails; read audioFailure() (ZenScript: audioError). Audio-only output failure is fatal.

Handle loading and errors

Status names are LOADING, READY, PLAYING, PAUSED, ENDED, FAILED and CLOSED. Read a fresh status() snapshot for position and retained errors. play resumes a paused player and restarts an ended player. seek cancels the old generation before publishing a new one; old decoder callbacks cannot replace new frames. Looping restarts at zero through the same mechanism. After a fatal failure, inspect the cause and use an explicit seek to start a new attempt; pause/play cannot hide the failed state.

A player keeps at most three queued CPU frames and uploads only changed frames. GPU upload, drawing and final closure run on Minecraft's client render thread. Downloading/decoding never allocates GPU resources. Close the player when its screen is disposed; the window also closes resources retained through ownVisual, including the ZenScript facade. Closure cancels decoding, terminates its owned processes, closes audio and deletes its texture. No media is registered globally or synchronized to the server.

Pass an AnimatedElement's local dimensions to player.draw inside its render callback to independently move, rotate, tint and fade that media layer. Keep controls in your screen's normal input handlers. For live feeds or another codec stack, implement MediaDecoder.Session: supply immutable timestamped CPU frames and optional signed little-endian 16-bit PCM, register every partially created resource in MediaCancellation, and respond to cancellation.
